transcript: Just got to see Two Strangers again. And can we talk about two strangers carry a cake across New York as a romcom through an ace aro lens? And spoilers for the musical if you have not seen it yet. I've seen people talk about how it's doesn't really fit to describe it as a romcom because they aren't in a strictly defined romantic relationship by the end of the show. But hear me out, because a romcom is just a formula, right? There's a meet cute, there's some conflict, and then there's the happily ever after. And many people describe the happily ever after as a coupling of sorts, right? They get together and then whatever happens, happens. But are all of the couples in romcoms really going to last? -debatable. I would argue that that happily ever after can just as easily be defined as two people realise that they have formed an everlasting connection. And that is absolutely what happens in two strangers. Two strangers has all of those things. It has a meet cute, it has conflict. And ultimately, and most importantly, both of these characters end up choosing each other in their own special way. And why I find this interesting as a musical through an ace aro lens is that's not to say that there is an attraction between these two characters. You can see and sense the tension and attraction between them. There's specific lines that I could point Out that definitely point to attraction between these two characters and signal something more. But what's important is that is not why they pick each other. In fact, in the first act, Robin chooses to hang out with Dougal over a sexual connection that she has with a stranger on Tinder. And in the second act, Dougal chooses to hang out with Robin over the very thing he came to New York to do. And whether or not there is that physical or romantic attraction between these two characters is up for debate. And whether or not there is physical intimacy is up for debate. The important thing, though, however, is that that's not what is important to the relationship. And the same could be said for ace and aro people, right? Some ace relationships do have that physical intimacy with a partner, some don't. The important thing, though, is that that's not what is important in that kind of relationship, because even if one of the people does have that physical attraction, that's not what that relationship is founded on. And that's very much the relationship in two strangers. Whether or not there is that physical intimacy is just. It's not important. At the end of the day, what is important is that they form this connection over these two magical days in New York and change each other for the better. And so, yeah, I would say because of these two days, they do get to live happily ever after. Whether that's with each other is up for interpretation, and I think that's beautiful. So, yeah, I consider two strangers a romcom, and I think you all should see it before November 29th.
showTitle: Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York)
classificationReason: Creator just attended the show again ('just got to see Two Strangers again') and shares opinions on the musical's genre and ace/aro representation, expressing clear enthusiasm ('I love Two Strangers').
